key_insight: By choosing the quantum-channel unraveling wisely, the average magic in noisy random circuits can be reduced, but a broad tail of high-magic trajectories still remains and limits stabilizer-based simulation gains.
engineering_relevance: For quantum simulators and error-aware compilers, this shows that measurement/noise representation can materially change classical simulability estimates even when observable averages are unchanged.
method: Study noisy Haar-random and T-doped random Clifford brickwork circuits with local dephasing.
Scan the full two-parameter family of minimal Kraus unravelings, including weak-measurement choices.
Quantify trajectory non-stabilizerness using stabilizer Rényi entropy and compare to Pauli-jump and projective-measurement limits.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that an optimal state-independent weak-measurement unraveling lowers the trajectory-averaged magic by a p-dependent factor while preserving linear scaling with system size, but leaves a sizable fraction of trajectories near Haar-random magic.
watch_item: Reducing the mean magic is not enough for simulation speedups, because rare high-magic trajectories can dominate stabilizer-method cost.
paper_title: Magic in quantum trajectory unravelings of noisy random quantum circuits
